summary.title: Out of Sight but Not Out of Mind: Hybrid Memory for Dynamic Video World Models

setting_and_object.category: Dataset + Algorithm (benchmark dataset and memory architecture for video world models)

details: Existing memory mechanisms for video world models treat the world as a static canvas, so dynamic subjects that leave the camera's field of view and return are rendered frozen, distorted, or vanish.
The paper formulates 'Hybrid Memory': simultaneously anchoring static background geometry and extrapolating the unseen motion/identity of dynamic subjects during out-of-view intervals.

HM-World: a large-scale synthetic video dataset (59K clips) purpose-built for hybrid memory, with camera trajectories deliberately decoupled from subject trajectories to induce dense subject exit-and-re-entry events.

HyDRA: a memory architecture that compresses context latents into spatiotemporal memory tokens via a 3D-convolutional memory tokenizer, then replaces 3D self-attention with retrieval attention that scores query-memory affinity and attends only to the top-k most relevant memory tokens plus a local temporal window.

Rendered in Unreal Engine 5 by combinatorially crossing 17 stylistically diverse scenes, 49 subjects (humans and animals) grouped 1-3 at a time, 10 predefined subject motion paths, and 28 camera trajectories with back-and-forth motions plus multiple start positions.
Clips lacking exit-entry events filtered out, yielding 59,225 clips annotated with MiniCPM-V captions, camera poses, per-frame subject positions, and exit/entry timestamps.

Compared against prior datasets (WorldScore, Context-as-Memory, Multi-Cam Video, 360-Motion) as the only one combining dynamic subjects, subject exit-enter events, subject poses, and a movable camera.
Built on Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B (causal 3D VAE + DiT, flow matching velocity prediction); camera poses flattened to f x 12 and injected via an MLP encoder added to latent features (ReCamMaster style).
77 context frames, temporally downsampled 4x by the VAE; memory tokenizer 3D conv kernel 2x4x4; retrieval top-k = 10 tokens; local denoising window = 5.
10K iterations on 32 GPUs, total batch size 32.
1000 held-out HM-World samples including scenes and subjects unseen in training.

Metrics: PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS for reconstruction fidelity; VBench Subject and Background Consistency; plus a new Dynamic Subject Consistency metric (YOLOv11 subject boxes, CLIP features of cropped regions, cosine similarity against GT video and against context video: DSC_GT and DSC_ctx).
Open-domain qualitative test on internet videos with imposed back-and-forth camera motion.

Baselines trained on HM-World under identical configs: naive concat baseline (context latents concatenated to noisy latents), DFoT, Context-as-Memory; plus zero-shot evaluation of the commercial WorldPlay model.

Ablations: memory tokenizer kernel size (temporal 1 vs 2; spatial 2x2 / 4x4 / 8x8), number of retrieved tokens (5/10/15), and retrieval criterion (dynamic feature affinity vs FOV-overlap geometric retrieval), including analysis of retrieved-token distribution across DiT layers and timesteps.

key_findings.finding: HyDRA substantially improves both dynamic-subject and overall consistency over static-centric memory methods on hybrid-memory scenarios.
key_findings.evidence: On the 1000-sample HM-World test set, HyDRA reaches PSNR 20.357 / SSIM 0.606 / LPIPS 0.289 versus 18.696 / 0.517 / 0.356 for the concat baseline, 18.921 / 0.530 / 0.342 for Context-as-Memory, and 17.693 / 0.482 / 0.410 for DFoT; DSC_ctx 0.827 and DSC_GT 0.849 are also highest, with Subject/Background Consistency 0.926/0.932. Qualitatively, baselines and Context-as-Memory show subject distortion, DFoT loses the subject entirely.

key_findings.finding: Feature-level dynamic affinity retrieval beats FOV-overlap geometric retrieval because it adapts per layer and per timestep rather than fixing a token set.
key_findings.evidence: Swapping in FOV-overlap retrieval drops PSNR to 19.776 and Subject Consistency to 0.908 (vs 20.357 / 0.926); visualizations show FOV retrieval selects the nearest-pose but empty shots and yields an identical fixed token selection across denoising, whereas dynamic affinity retrieves subject-containing keyframes with a diverse selection distribution.

key_findings.finding: Temporal interaction inside the memory tokenizer is the critical design element, while spatial compression ratio matters little.
key_findings.evidence: Reducing the tokenizer temporal kernel from 2 to 1 costs 1.281 PSNR (20.357 to 19.076) and 0.014 DSC_GT, whereas changing spatial kernel from 4x4 to 2x2 or 8x8 changes PSNR by only 0.244 and 0.127; qualitative results with temporal kernel 1 show inconsistent subjects.

key_findings.finding: A moderate retrieved-token budget is both necessary and sufficient, with too few tokens causing hallucination.
key_findings.evidence: Top-k = 5 gives PSNR 19.309 and DSC_GT 0.836 with artifacts such as duplicating a single giraffe into two, while k = 10 and k = 15 are near-identical (PSNR 20.357 vs 20.333), indicating extra tokens add redundant noise rather than information.

key_findings.finding: Even a strong commercial video world model lacks specialized hybrid memory, though its behavior validates the proposed DSC metric.
key_findings.evidence: Zero-shot WorldPlay scores PSNR 14.855 / SSIM 0.355 / DSC_GT 0.832 versus HyDRA's 20.357 / 0.606 / 0.849, yet attains a comparatively robust context-referenced DSC_ctx of 0.822 while exhibiting stuttering, unnatural subject motion in qualitative comparisons.
